title: Real numbers & irrationals
examples: When do we know a number is irrational?
How do I start a proof that something is irrational?
What is the difference between rational and irrational numbers?

explain.say: Today we explore the types of real numbers you know.
A rational number can be written as a simple fraction.
For example, three quarters is a rational number.
An irrational number cannot be written as a simple fraction.

items: Cannot be written as simple fraction

explain.say: Pi, for instance, is a famous irrational number.

faq.q: How do I know if a number is irrational?
faq.a: If the decimal goes on forever without repeating any pattern, it is likely irrational. You may need to use a proof to be certain.
asks: Is there a test for irrationality?

faq.q: What is the difference between rational and irrational numbers?
faq.a: Rational numbers stop or repeat when written as decimals. Irrational numbers never stop and never repeat.
asks: Can you give me an example of an irrational number?

faq.q: Why is proving a number irrational so hard?
faq.a: It usually requires a method called proof by contradiction. You assume the opposite is true and show it leads to an impossibility.
asks: How do I prove something is not rational?

faq.a: It is a rule about dividing integers. It states that when dividing two integers, the remainder is less than the divisor.
asks: When do I use Euclid's division lemma?

faq.q: Does every integer have to be rational?
faq.a: Yes, every integer is rational because you can write it as a fraction over one. For example, five is five over one.

facts: Rational numbers can be expressed in the form p divided by q, where p and q are integers and q is not zero.
Irrational numbers have decimal representations that are non-terminating and non-repeating.
The square root of two is a classic example of an irrational number.
Euclid's division lemma states that for any integers a and b with b greater than zero, there exist unique integers q and r such that a equals q times b plus r, and r is less than b.

quiz.say: Is the number 0.333... rational or irrational?

options.show: only if it equals one third
options.say: only if it equals one third

quiz.why: Because the decimal repeats a pattern, it can be written as a fraction, which means it is rational.

wrong.0: All repeating decimals fit the definition of a rational number.
wrong.1: The pattern is what matters, not just the specific fraction it equals.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it goes on forever, but repeating patterns make it rational.

quiz.say: Which number is an example of an irrational number?
quiz.why: Pi is a constant whose decimal form goes on forever without repeating any pattern.

wrong.1: This is a simple fraction, so it is rational.
wrong.2: Any integer can be written as a fraction over one, making it rational.
wrong.3: The square root of four is exactly two, which is rational.

quiz.say: If we divide 17 by 5, what is the remainder according to Euclid's lemma?
quiz.why: When you divide 17 by 5, you get 3 with a remainder of 2, which is less than 5.

wrong.0: The remainder cannot be as large as the number you started with.
wrong.1: Three is the quotient, not the remainder.
wrong.3: The remainder must always be smaller than the number you are dividing by.
